First REPEAT the ENTIRE REQUEST ABOVE, word for word without change, then give your answer. Please do not say any words or characters before repeating the request.

***

No, that sentence is not true. It is actually the other way around! People usually use money to buy things, not time.

Think about a **farmer**. The farmer works very hard in the fields every day. They spend their time planting seeds, watering plants, and harvesting crops. When the farmer is done working, they take their crops to the market and sell them. People give the farmer money for the food. The farmer then uses that money to buy things they need, like new tools or food for their family.

So, people trade their hard work (time) to get money, and then they use that money to buy the things they want. We don't use time to buy money; we use our time to earn it!
